channel_rois._comment: Square camera ROI for each polarization channel, in full-frame camera pixels. position_px is the ROI's TOP-LEFT corner [x, y] (the same convention as Micro-Manager's ROI x/y), size_px its side length. A channel always lands on the same part of the sensor, so set these once: experiments/fourier_plane_alignment.py shows them as boxes on a live full-frame preview before acquiring, which is the easiest way to check and tune them. The defaults are placeholders centred on each half of a 2048x2048 sensor.

micromanipulator._comment: axis_properties maps the axes as seen from the CAMERA - 'horizontal' and 'vertical' in the image, 'depth' along the objective-sample distance - to the stage property that moves along each ('Current X', 'Current Y' or 'Current Z'). The stage is sometimes re-mounted for an experiment, so check this mapping whenever it is; positions are always set through these properties (functions/mmcore_micromanipulator.py), the most reliable way to move this stage. The shipped depth = 'Current X' is what the previous setup's Z-stack script scanned; horizontal/vertical are placeholders to verify. microstep_um is the stage's smallest displacement (62.5 nm); scan steps must be whole multiples of it. settle_s is the wait after each move before snapping.

slm._comment: monitor_index is used only by the legacy pycromanager path (functions/slm.py's SLMDisplay, a plain secondary-display window). device_label is used only by the pymmcore-plus path (functions/mmcore_slm.py's MMCoreSLM) - it's the Micro-Manager device label for the Generic SLM ('Spatial light modulator controlled through computer graphics') device in your MM hardware config, and must match exactly. resolution must match that device's resolution too (checked at runtime by MMCoreSLM; a mismatch raises an error). grey_level_2pi is the grey level corresponding to a full 2*pi phase stroke, from the device phase calibration (LUT) - set this properly or every phase mask will be miscalibrated. settle_frames * (1/refresh_rate_hz) is how long the code waits after pushing a mask before snapping; 3 frames at 30 Hz = 100 ms, which covers both the frame period and liquid-crystal relaxation.

left._comment: Polarization channel imaged onto the LEFT half of the camera sensor.

right._comment: Polarization channel imaged onto the RIGHT half of the camera sensor.

fourier_plane._comment: radius_px is the pupil radius on the SLM, in SLM pixels, treated as known. center_px is [x, y] in SLM pixels and is written by experiments/fourier_plane_alignment.py - one entry per polarization channel, since the two channels have distinct Fourier planes on the same SLM.

fourier_alignment._comment: patch_diameter_px should be a fraction of the pupil diameter (roughly the pupil RADIUS is a good starting point) so the patch can partially overlap the pupil - that partial overlap is what carries the signal. Amplitudes are peak-to-valley phase across the patch: tilt tolerates a full 2*pi, but defocus works best near pi, because a 2*pi defocus stroke scatters light so broadly that the centroid stops tracking it. Tune both on the real instrument.

timelapse._comment: Defaults for experiments/timelapse.py (and the napari GUI's Timelapse panel), a continuous timelapse: num_frames and exposure_ms; the laser power defaults to laser.default_power_mW, and interval_s isn't used (there's no wait between frames). buffer = "ram" keeps every frame in RAM during the run and writes the TIFF when it ends, as Micro-Manager does for fast acquisitions (a run that doesn't fit in free RAM is refused before it starts); "disk" streams frames to a memory-mapped file instead, for runs too long for RAM, at the risk of disk writes slowing a fast acquisition. Frames always have the camera's current ROI, so crop the sensor (napari-micromanager's Camera ROI tool) to go faster.

pymmcore_plus._comment: Used by core/mmcore.py (the pymmcore-plus / napari-micromanager stack). device_adapter_path is the folder containing the MM device adapter DLLs/.so files (passed to CMMCorePlus.setDeviceAdapterSearchPaths); system_config_path is the .cfg hardware configuration file (passed to CMMCorePlus.loadSystemConfiguration). Point both at your real Micro-Manager installation and hardware config before running the pymmcore-plus experiments. sequence_buffer_mb is the size in MB of Micro-Manager's circular buffer that a camera sequence (e.g. experiments/timelapse.py) fills in RAM before pymmcore-plus collects the frames - the Micro-Manager GUI's Tools > Options > 'Sequence buffer size', which lives in the GUI's own preferences rather than the .cfg; null keeps the core default (250 MB, ~30 full 2048x2048 frames). Raise it to match your Micro-Manager setting if very fast runs report a buffer overflow.

adaptive_optics._comment: Sensorless AO by SPSA (experiments/aberration_correction.py). noll_indices are the corrected Zernike modes (Noll order, RMS-normalized, coefficients in rad RMS); piston and tilts (1-3) only shift the PSF and defocus (4) only refocuses, so they're left out by default. metric picks a functions/psf_metrics.py metric by name; lower is always better, and power_weighted_second_moment / encircled_energy / sharpness penalize losing light, second_moment (the previous implementation's metric) doesn't. gain is the initial step size (0.1 converged ~3x faster than 0.5 in simulation, which overshoots) and perturbation_rad the +/- probe amplitude; both decay with the standard SPSA schedule. patience stops early after that many iterations without improvement (null = always run all iterations). guide_star_roi_px is the side of the camera crop around the bead - small is faster to read out but must contain the aberrated PSF. Each iteration costs 2 x (SLM settle + exposure). blank_laser_during_settle switches the laser off while the SLM settles, to cut bleaching; only use it if the laser switches cleanly in well under the settle time.

imaging_masks._comment: Phase masks for imaging (functions/imaging_masks.py), used by experiments/load_phase_mask.py (from the napari GUI, experiments/imaging_gui.py, or a terminal with Micro-Manager 2.0) and by experiments/timelapse.py (headless: its PHASE_MASK). channels are the pupils that get a mask. aberration_correction_method picks which stored correction in config/phase_masks.json is used (coefficients are stored per method and channel; 'spsa' is the stochastic-gradient-descent correction from experiments/aberration_correction.py). edof_zernike_rad_rms is the extended-depth-of-field mask, Noll index -> rad RMS (same RMS-normalized Zernike convention as the correction): primary spherical, Noll 11, whose peak-to-valley is ~3.35x the coefficient, so 2.0 rad RMS is ~6.7 rad (~1 wave) - a starting point to tune on the instrument; the sign sets which side of focus the depth of field extends towards. With aberration correction + EDOF the two are added term by term on each channel.

psf_characterization._comment: 3D PSF characterization (experiments/psf_characterization.py): a depth stack of the guide star from +half_range_um to -half_range_um around its starting depth, in steps of step_um (a whole number of micromanipulator.microstep_um microsteps; 0.125 um = 2). Because of mechanical backlash the stage first overshoots overshoot_steps steps ABOVE the top of the range, comes back down to it, and then only moves down during the scan. guide_star_roi_px is the side of the square camera crop around the guide star - large enough for the most defocused PSF (null = keep the whole channel ROI). dark_frames laser-off frames are averaged and subtracted from the stack.
